title: DDoS Protection | How It Works and How to Protect Against DDoS Attacks
content_md: DDoS protection combines tools and techniques to detect and filter malicious traffic from a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack before it overwhelms a website, server, or network. It identifies attack traffic, absorbs or scrubs it away from your infrastructure, and lets legitimate requests through, usually automatically and within seconds. The need is no longer occasional. Cloudflare reported mitigating 23.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks in the first half of 2026 alone, roughly 5,300 attacks per hour. This guide explains how DDoS protection works, the types available, and how to protect a website, server, or network of any size. What Is DDoS Protection? DDoS protection is the set of defenses that keeps a website, server, or network online during a distributed denial-of-service attack. It detects malicious traffic and filters it out before it reaches your infrastructure. Its goal is availability: legitimate users keep getting through while attackers flood the target with junk requests. It can be delivered as a cloud service, on-premises hardware, or a mix of both.
